column1: # Game profile of Mario Party Superstars (Switch, update 1.1.1 = v131072). Plays on the Mac: a board and a minigame
# NintendoWare Bezel Engine, SDK 11.4.3: RomFS is 477 Bezel Engine archives (.bea) beside 209 .bfstm streams; the shaders are BNSH, 80,783 in Archive/, 1,936 in the engine's System.nx.bea
# and 71 in main (82,790: 52,241 pixel, 30,514 vertex, 23 compute, 12 geometry). The boards, minigames and menus
# are 126 NROs (nro/NX_Release/hsbd*, hsmg*, hsmn*, registered by .nrr/hs.nrr), loaded with ro::LoadModule

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = GLSLC, subsdk1 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false and main sets a heap of the pool − 64 MB (3.14 GB in a 3.25 GB heap region; about 2.3 GB resident on a board)
# the game sets the near = 0 depth mode (nvnDeviceSetDepthMode): the pipeline bases made before it runs take the main0_z vertex entries
# the materials' clustered lights keep their shadow maps' and projected textures' handles in a storage buffer, past the translator's fallback arrays: those 6,370 shaders load
# with neutral textures, so the lights draw without shadows or projected textures (nvn_mtl.m white_tex; docs/reference/shaders.md, Texture handles from the game's own data)
